drhp.business: PNC Media and Entertainment Limited (formerly Pritish Nandy Communications Limited) produces original web series and films commissioned by or pre-sold to global streaming platforms, and monetises its content library through licensing to broadcasters and streaming platforms. It operates through two subsidiaries: PNC Digital Limited, positioned as a distribution intermediary for the streaming business, and PNC Wellness Limited, a dormant former wellness-centre operator.
drhp.expansion: No physical capacity expansion is disclosed; the Company's expansion activity is content-pipeline based — Season 2 of The Royals is in pre-production, scheduled to begin filming in Q2 of the current financial year, and the Company intends to put at least two more productions (new series/films) on the floors later this financial year.

litigation.note: The Company received a 2016 arbitration award in its favour against White Feather Films (Proprietor Mr Sanjay Gupta); the matter was later settled via consent terms filed before the Bombay High Court, which accepted the terms by order dated April 21, 2026 (read in the MD&A and Board's Report).

risks.note: Shifting audience tastes and lifestyle patterns make the theatrical market for films unpredictable, and distributors/studios are risk-averse, reluctant to pay minimum guarantees upfront.

The Company currently mitigates this by making content that is pre-sold or commissioned, but may in future make small IPR-stake investments in shows/films once the market normalises, reintroducing recovery risk.
Includes injury to lead actors/technical crew, loss by fire, high personnel turnover, piracy, delay in production cycles for reasons beyond the Company's control, and censor certification issues.
Flagged among operational risks alongside statutory and legal compliance exposure.

risks.note: Shortage of working capital, diminution of asset values, data loss, inventory loss, bad debts, and theft/loss of cash and valuables.
Piracy and misuse of intellectual property rights, and injury to the PNC brand image.
The Company's archived filmed content is ageing and, in the current digital scenario, risks becoming technology-obsolete; mitigated by digitising the entire films archive.
Flagged as an operational risk requiring continuous anticipation of trends and updating of technological skills to meet a maturing viewership's rising quality expectations.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Global content consumption is rising, with a new generation of Indian viewers increasingly watching global content on streaming platforms.
- The theatrical market for films remains unpredictable due to shifting audience tastes and lifestyle patterns; distributors and studios are risk-averse and reluctant to pay minimum guarantees upfront.
- A maturing viewership expects progressively higher content-quality standards, requiring continuous technological and trend-anticipation updates.
- If and when the market returns to normal, the Company may consider small investments for a stake in IPR on shows and films, rather than remaining fully pre-sold/commissioned.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: No physical capacity expansion is disclosed; the Company's expansion activity is content-pipeline based — Season 2 of The Royals is in pre-production, scheduled to begin filming in Q2 of the current financial year, and the Company intends to put at least two more productions (new series/films) on the floors later this financial year.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Shifting audience tastes and lifestyle patterns make the theatrical market for films unpredictable, and distributors/studios are risk-averse, reluctant to pay minimum guarantees upfront.
- The Company currently mitigates this by making content that is pre-sold or commissioned, but may in future make small IPR-stake investments in shows/films once the market normalises, reintroducing recovery risk.
- Includes injury to lead actors/technical crew, loss by fire, high personnel turnover, piracy, delay in production cycles for reasons beyond the Company's control, and censor certification issues.
- Flagged among operational risks alongside statutory and legal compliance exposure.
- Shortage of working capital, diminution of asset values, data loss, inventory loss, bad debts, and theft/loss of cash and valuables.
- Piracy and misuse of intellectual property rights, and injury to the PNC brand image.
- The Company's archived filmed content is ageing and, in the current digital scenario, risks becoming technology-obsolete; mitigated by digitising the entire films archive.
- Flagged as an operational risk requiring continuous anticipation of trends and updating of technological skills to meet a maturing viewership's rising quality expectations.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Scale up the existing business primarily by continuing to create new content (original series and movies) that top-rated global studios are willing to financially and operationally collaborate on.
- Leverage the content library across various platforms on a global scale.
- Focus on entirely de-risked strategies for recovering investments in content, currently making content that is pre-sold or commissioned rather than self-funded.
- Use PNC Digital Limited to explore distribution-intermediary opportunities for content makers shifting from traditional media to digital.
- Digitised the entire films archive to keep older filmed content usable on current satellite and streaming platforms.
